paper.title: Provably Efficient Online Hyperparameter Optimization with Population-Based Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Parallel (batch) time-varying Gaussian process bandit optimization for online hyperparameter selection
unmapped: Reward function evolves as a time-varying GP: f_{t+1} = sqrt(1-omega) f_t + sqrt(omega) g_{t+1}, g ~ GP(0,k), with forgetting parameter omega in [0,1] (Bogunovic et al. 2016 model)
Population of B parallel agents choose a batch of B points each round; batch regret uses the best point in the batch (max over b)
settings.definition_quote: We formulate this problem as optimizing the time-varying black-box reward function $f_t$, over $\mathcal{D}$. Every $t_{\mathrm{ready}}$ steps, we observe and record noisy observations, $y_t = f_t(x_t) + \epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2\mathbf{I})$ ... f_{t+1}(x) = \sqrt{1-\omega}f_t(x) + \sqrt{\omega}g_{t+1}(x)

bound.regime: any block length N_tilde in {1,...,T}, B << T

symbols.beta_T: 2 log(pi^2 T^2/(2 delta)) + 2 d log(r d b T^2 sqrt(log(d a pi^2 T^2/(2 delta))))
symbols.N_tilde: block length for the time-varying information gain bound
symbols.gamma_NB: maximum information gain of the (time-invariant) kernel after N_tilde*B_pop points
symbols.omega: forgetting/time-variation parameter of the time-varying GP
symbols.r: side length of the box [0,r]^d containing the domain

conditions: domain D subset [0,r]^d compact and convex
f_t ~ GP(0,k) almost surely continuously differentiable
p(sup |df_t/dx^(j)| >= L) <= a exp(-(L/b)^2) for all L >= 0
regret per round measured using the best agent in the batch: f_t(x_t^*) - max_b f_t(x_{t,b})
tuning: beta_T = 2 log(pi^2 T^2/(2 delta)) + 2 d log(r d b T^2 sqrt(log(d a pi^2 T^2/(2 delta))))

source.quote: Let the domain $\mathcal{D}\subset[0,r]^{d}$ be compact and convex ... Pick $\delta\in(0,1)$, set $\beta_{T}=...$ and define $C_{1}=32/\log(1+\sigma_{f}^{2})$, the PB2 algorithm satisfies the following regret bound after $T$ time steps over $B$ parallel agents with probability at least $1-\delta$: R_{TB}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}f_{t}(\bx_{t}^{*})-\max_{b=1,...,B} f_{t}(\bx_{t,b})\le \sqrt{C_{1}T\beta_{T}\left(\frac{T}{\tilde{N}B}+1\right)\left(\gamma_{\tilde{N}B}+\left[\tilde{N}B\right]^{3}\omega\right)}+2 the bound holds for any block length $\tilde{N}\in\left\{ 1,...,T\right\}$ and $B\ll T$.

results.notes: Restated identically as Theorem 12 (label main_theorem) in the appendix. The proof's final line actually has an extra 1/B factor and a 1/sigma_f^2 factor on the omega term, and C_1 is written inconsistently (log(1+sigma_f^{-2}) vs log(1+sigma_f^2)); recorded as stated in the theorem. The proof also specialises to the SE kernel with gamma replaced by (d+1)log(N_tilde B). 'B << T' is a vague condition. Environment mapped to nonstationary_drifting as the closest fit for the time-varying GP model.
